**Proposed mechanism:** Pathogenic variant in FLNC (HGNC:3715) —DISRUPTS→ Filamin C (HGNC:3715); Filamin C (HGNC:3715) —DISRUPTS→ Cardiac muscle cytoskeletal integrity (GO:0003010); Cardiac muscle cytoskeletal integrity (GO:0003010) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (MONDO:0004994); Pathogenic variant in FLNC (HGNC:3715) —DISRUPTS→ Filamin C (HGNC:3715); Filamin C (HGNC:3715) —DISRUPTS→ Peripheral nerve cytoskeletal integrity (GO:0007010); Peripheral nerve cytoskeletal integrity (GO:0007010) —LEADS_TO→ Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 4K (MONDO:0014733). Pathogenic variants in FLNC disrupt the function of Filamin C, a protein crucial for cytoskeletal organization. In the heart, this leads to impaired cardiac muscle cytoskeletal integrity and cardiomyopathy. In peripheral nerves, disruption of FLNC affects neuronal cytoskeletal integrity, resulting in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 4K. Both diseases converge on the shared mechanism of compromised cytoskeletal integrity due to FLNC dysfunction.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in FLNC that segregate with Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 4K but not with cardiomyopathy, or vice versa, would falsify this hypothesis. Additionally, demonstrating distinct functional consequences of FLNC variants in cardiac versus neuronal tissues that cannot be explained by tissue-specific roles in cytoskeletal maintenance would also be falsifying. _(variant: The presence of common variants in FLNC with a minor allele frequency >0.1% in gnomAD that are associated with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of FLNC in both cardiac and neurological tissues could lead to the development of therapies targeting cytoskeletal maintenance that benefit patients with both cardiomyopathy and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 4K, or related disorders.
